title: Jonah and the Postcards
premise: Emrys Sandoval, a celebrated restaurant critic who lost the ability to taste after a childhood rupture no one in the family will name, returns to the coastal town of Porthaven when their grandmother's house is scheduled for demolition. At the funeral of Great-Aunt Bess, a stranger named Delphine addresses the family as 'the Merrows'—a surname that appears on a cache of unsent postcards hidden in the walls, each one written by a different relative to a person none of them can identify. As Emrys catalogs the postcards and interviews the scattered family, they uncover that decades ago the family split into two names to hide a betrayal over the original family restaurant, and that Emrys's tastelessness began the day they were made complicit in the silence. The demolition date forces a reckoning: at a final dinner cooked from the old restaurant's recovered recipes, Emrys tastes again for the first time, the family chooses one name—their true one—and the house comes down with everyone watching, together.
about_author: Wren Voss is the pen name of a former line cook who spent six years writing menu copy before turning to fiction. They live near the sea and collect postcards they never send.

chapters.title: The Smile That Ends Conversations
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. In London, Emrys files a glowing review of food they cannot taste, then learns of Great-Aunt Bess's death and the demolition order on the Porthaven house. The beat is hollow competence masking grief.

chapters.title: Strangers at the Funeral
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. At Bess's funeral, a woman named Delphine greets the mourners as 'the Merrows,' and every relative goes still. Emrys, professionally observant, notices who avoids whose eyes. Beat: a crack in the family's polished surface.

chapters.title: What the Walls Kept
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Clearing the house, Emrys finds forty-one unsent postcards sealed inside a kitchen wall, all addressed to someone called only 'M.' Each is in different handwriting. Beat: curiosity overtaking dread.

chapters.title: Aunt Vera Declines to Comment
chapters.summary: Vera's POV. The imperious eldest aunt deflects Emrys's questions over tea, revealing she knew about the postcards and chose the wall herself. Beat: loyalty as a form of imprisonment.

chapters.title: Delphine at the Door
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Delphine arrives claiming to be Bess's goddaughter and a Merrow by blood; the cousins split over whether to let her stay. Beat: the outsider as mirror.

chapters.title: Recipes Without a Restaurant
chapters.summary: Delphine's POV. Delphine cooks an old family dish in the dying house; Emrys watches, tasting nothing, and lies about it. Beat: shame sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Year of Two Names
chapters.summary: Uncle Theo's POV. Theo recalls 1974, when half the family took the name Sandoval after a fire closed the original restaurant, the Merrow's Table. He stops short of saying why. Beat: the past pressing through the seams.

chapters.title: Postcards to M.
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Reading the postcards chronologically, Emrys maps a decades-long conversation between siblings that ended mid-sentence in 1975. Beat: intimacy found in other people's unsent words.

chapters.title: Cousin Idris Comes Home
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. The estranged cousin returns for his inheritance, weaponizing the family's secrets against them. Beat: resentment wearing charm.

chapters.title: What Emrys Stopped Tasting
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. A flashback chapter: nine-year-old Emrys witnesses the family argument that renamed them all, and swallows their questions along with a last meal they cannot remember. Beat: the origin of silence.

chapters.title: Vera Breaks a Plate
chapters.summary: Vera's POV. Confronted by Idris with a photograph, Vera shatters her composure and admits the fire was set deliberately—by whom, she still won't say. Beat: guilt curdling into fury.

chapters.title: The Demolition Notice
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The council confirms the demolition date: three weeks. Emrys realizes the house itself is the last witness. Beat: a clock starts ticking.

chapters.title: Delphine's Version
chapters.summary: Delphine's POV. Delphine reveals her grandmother was the sibling erased from every story—the cook whose recipes became the restaurant, and who was blamed for the fire. Beat: sympathy complicating allegiance.

chapters.title: Theo's Confession, Half-Finished
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo begins confessing his role in the cover-up but collapses mid-sentence, hospitalized. Beat: the cost of carrying secrets alone.

chapters.title: Idris Sells the Story
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Idris leaks the family scandal to a local paper, threatening the demolition delay Emrys had petitioned for. Beat: betrayal inside the family circle.

chapters.title: Reading Aloud
chapters.summary: Ensemble scene, Emrys's POV. Trapped together by a storm, the family reads the postcards aloud; each recognizes their own handwriting and their own omissions. Beat: collective reckoning, tender and raw.

chapters.title: The Last Postcard
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Behind the oven, Emrys finds postcard forty-two, signed by Bess to 'M'—her sister Marisol, Delphine's grandmother—with an apology and a recipe. Beat: the missing piece arriving too late and exactly on time.

chapters.title: Who Set the Fire
chapters.summary: Vera's POV. Vera finally names the arsonist: not Marisol but the patriarch, to claim insurance and erase his sister's partnership. Beat: the founding lie exposed.

chapters.title: One Table
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys proposes a final dinner before demolition, cooked from Marisol's recovered recipe book, with both halves of the family and Delphine at one table. Preparations expose old wounds. Beat: fragile hope.

chapters.title: The Dinner
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The dinner nearly collapses under accusation until Emrys serves the first course and—tasting it—begins to weep. The flavor returns. Beat: climax; the senses and the family restored together.

chapters.title: One Name
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Around the emptied table, the family votes to reclaim 'Merrow' as their shared name; even Idris signs the petition delaying nothing but changing everything. Beat: chosen identity over inherited silence.

chapters.title: Watching It Come Down
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The family stands together as the house falls; Emrys mails the forty-two postcards at last, addressed to living descendants, keeping only Bess's. Final beat: memory released, appetite for life returned.
